methodology: Editorial era filters may overlap. All bounds are inclusive. Day-precision concert dates follow titled source dates, not timezone-shifted CMS metadata. Month/year bounds support navigation and must not be interpreted as exact membership dates. Personnel windows indicate association with the performing ensemble, not confirmed attendance. Nonperforming lyricists and sporadic guests are outside this initial filter catalog.

eras.title: Acid Tests & beginnings
eras.description: An exploratory lens on the Warlocks-to-Grateful Dead transition and the Acid Test years. Calendar-year boundaries are editorial.

eras.title: Psychedelic expansion
eras.description: An editorial window onto an expanding ensemble and extended improvisation. It overlaps personnel changes rather than defining a fixed lineup.

eras.title: Acoustic & electric roots
eras.description: An editorial window around Workingman’s Dead, American Beauty, and the acoustic/electric repertoire.

eras.title: Europe ’72
eras.description: The European tour, bounded by its opening and final concerts.

eras.title: Wall of Sound
eras.description: The 1974 touring system, from the Cow Palace sound test to the Winterland farewell run. Earlier prototypes are outside this filter.

eras.title: Touring hiatus
eras.description: The break from regular touring. The band continued recording and played several concerts in 1975; this is not a period without performances.

eras.title: Return to the road
eras.description: The post-hiatus period through Keith and Donna’s last concert. The label describes this project’s chosen date window.

eras.title: Brent years
eras.description: A lineup lens spanning Brent Mydland’s first and final concerts with the band.

eras.title: Vince years
eras.description: The final keyboard era, with Vince Welnick and recurring guest Bruce Hornsby during part of the period.

events.title: The Grateful Dead name
events.description: The band began appearing under its new name at the December 1965 Acid Tests. Date shown is a month-level marker.

events.title: A second drummer
events.description: Mickey Hart joined in September 1967. The month marker avoids conflicting first-show dates.

events.title: Tom Constanten joins the touring band
events.description: Constanten’s keyboard work became part of the touring ensemble in November.

events.title: Workingman’s Dead & American Beauty
events.description: The two 1970 studio albums form a useful landmark for exploring the roots-oriented repertoire. This marker represents the year, not either release day.

events.title: Mickey steps away
events.description: Hart left the road in February; Bill Kreutzmann continued on drums. The date is a month-level marker.

events.title: Keith’s first concert
events.description: Northrop Auditorium introduced Keith Godchaux onstage. The official show notes also identify first performances of Jack Straw and Tennessee Jed.

events.title: Donna joins the regular stage lineup
events.description: Donna Jean’s regular participation began before Europe ’72, following a brief New Year’s Eve appearance.

events.title: Europe ’72 begins
events.description: The European tour ran from April 7 through May 26.

events.title: Pigpen’s final concert; Stella Blue debuts
events.description: The Hollywood Bowl show notes identify Pigpen’s last appearance and the first Stella Blue.

events.title: Wall of Sound test; Scarlet Begonias debuts
events.description: The Cow Palace show is documented as the Wall’s sound test and the first performances of Scarlet Begonias and Cassidy.

events.title: Winterland farewell & Mickey’s return
events.description: The final Winterland farewell concert preceded the touring hiatus and brought Mickey Hart back onstage.

events.title: A quieter year, not a silent one
events.description: The band worked on Blues for Allah and played several public concerts during the touring hiatus. This marker represents the year.

events.title: Touring resumes
events.description: The band returned to the road at Portland’s Paramount Theatre.

events.title: Fire on the Mountain debuts
events.description: The Winterland show notes identify the first Fire on the Mountain.

events.title: Keith & Donna’s last concert
events.description: The Oakland benefit show closed their performing tenure with the band.

events.title: Brent’s first concert
events.description: Brent Mydland made his concert debut after Keith and Donna’s departure.

events.title: Brent’s final concert
events.description: Mydland’s final concert took place at the World Music Theatre in Tinley Park.

events.title: Vince’s first concert
events.description: Vince Welnick debuted at Richfield Coliseum.

events.title: Bruce begins his recurring touring role
events.description: Hornsby joined the fall touring lineup alongside Vince; this does not mark his first guest appearance with the band.

events.title: The final Grateful Dead concert
events.description: The band’s final concert took place at Soldier Field, Chicago.
